title: calibrate-serving-simulation
summary: Build an evidence-gated serving-configuration shortlist from a profiled simulator while separating empirical predictions from physical bounds and near-capacity queueing risk.

skill_metadata.name: calibrate-serving-simulation
skill_metadata.description: Build an evidence-gated serving-configuration shortlist from a profiled simulator while separating empirical predictions from physical bounds and near-capacity queueing risk.

applicability.scope: Building an evidence-gated serving-configuration shortlist when a profiled simulator or cost model is proposed to reduce deployment experiments; extends performance-ceiling-analysis, optimization-search-policy and inference-benchmark-design without replacing their ceilings or measurement contract
applicability.prerequisites: The packaged Vidur evidence and evidence-type notes are read; reading the skill does not authorize execution, and no validation check runs under it without separate execution authorization
applicability.input_contract: Model, shape and dtype; actual kernel/runtime revision; graph mode; GPU, host and topology; request length and arrival distribution; total resources and cost basis; memory limits; latency definitions and percentile SLOs
applicability.produced_artifact: A bounded decision memo with input identities, model assumptions, evidence type, exact metrics and denominators, unsupported dimensions, nondominated candidates with predicted ranges, joint constraint checks, the next discriminating trial and rollback/finalization requirements, keeping prediction and measurement columns apart; a shortlist for future measurement, not a measured result
failure_modes: Learned runtime output is labeled a physical bound
A missing identity is filled with a paper default, or topology is substituted, instead of being marked unknown
A low-load check stands in for an SLO claim at the intended load regime and capacity boundary
A predictor that relies on summed KV volume hides batches with equal volume but unequal context distributions
Capacity binary search is applied without verifying its monotonic/stationary premise or treating overloaded samples explicitly
One predicted winner is reported when uncertainty exceeds rank separation
applicability.refusal_point: Stops predictive certification when profiles are missing, topology is substituted, error grows near capacity or host overhead is omitted; labels an ordering unresolved when uncertainty exceeds rank separation; asserts neither universal error below 9% nor current vLLM, asynchronous PP or NPU support from the historical simulator paper

recommendations: Classify every estimate as a physical bound, measured envelope, Amdahl-style conditional impact or empirical prediction before comparing configurations.
Keep prefill and decode separate in the operator signatures, and record how sharding and memory planning enter the model.
Recalibrate after workload drift, kernel/graph/runtime changes, new hardware or topology, or mismatched residuals.
limitations: Source-derived candidate; no local efficacy validation.
